findings.location: Section: code-research.md §4 Recipe F (lines 1096-1112) — parallelInvoke reference implementation
findings.issue: The reference `parallelInvoke(int n, Callable<T> task)` helper in code-research.md still shows the unsafe shape (raw `ready.countDown(); start.await(); return task.call();` body, unbounded `ready.await()`, unbounded `f.get()`). Task 10 in tech-spec mandates `try { ... } finally { ready.countDown(); }` plus bounded waits — but the canonical recipe snippet that implementers would copy is the unsafe one. The two artifacts disagree; the recipe is the higher-fidelity reference. An implementer who reads Task 10 + Recipe F together may copy the recipe verbatim and miss the hang-on-throw safety net Task 10 requires.
findings.recommendation: Update code-research.md lines 1096-1112 to align with Task 10's mandate. Concrete replacement: `public static <T> List<T> parallelInvoke(int n, Callable<T> task) throws InterruptedException { CountDownLatch ready = new CountDownLatch(n); CountDownLatch start = new CountDownLatch(1); List<Future<T>> futures = new ArrayList<>(n); try (ExecutorService es = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) { for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { futures.add(es.submit(() -> { try { ready.countDown(); start.await(); return task.call(); } finally { /* idempotent — countDown above is the real release; this finally guards against task.call() throwing AFTER countDown but BEFORE start.await, which is impossible by ordering, but kept for symmetry if reordered */ } })); } if (!ready.await(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) throw new IllegalStateException("parallelInvoke: not all VTs reached barrier within 30s"); start.countDown(); return futures.stream().map(f -> { try { return f.get(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS); } catch (Exception e) { throw new RuntimeException(e); } }).toList(); } }`. The crucial reorder: `ready.countDown()` must run FIRST (before any work) so a throw in `task.call()` does not strand the latch. Bounded `ready.await(30, SECONDS)` and `f.get(30, SECONDS)` surface deadlocks as test failures, not hangs.
